docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text: VisualEyes is a browser-based application that converts 2D architectural floor plans (DXF format) into fully furnished, interactive 3D apartment walkthroughs. Targeted at the real estate industry, it enables property buyers to virtually walk through apartments before they are physically constructed.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: In the real estate market, buyers typically make major purchasing decisions based on flat 2D floor plans and static artist renderings. Commissioning custom 3D walkthroughs for every floor plan variant is expensive and slow, creating an information gap between builders and prospective buyers.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text:
VisualEyes automates the entire pipeline — from DXF floor plan to interactive 3D tour — running entirely in the browser with zero server infrastructure:

  1. Parse — Read a standard AutoCAD DXF file and extract walls, doors, and windows
  2. Detect — Identify closed room boundaries and classify room types (bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, etc.)
  3. Furnish — Auto-place contextually appropriate furniture in each room while respecting door swings and walkways
  4. Render — Generate a glTF/GLB 3D model with PBR materials, lighting, and shadows
  5. Tour — Present an interactive first-person walkthrough with room-by-room navigation and live customization

docs.title: Key Technical Decisions
docs.text: Decision Choice Rationale Runtime Pyodide (Python in WebAssembly) Leverages Python geometry/graph libraries (numpy, networkx, pydantic) client-side 3D Engine Three.js Industry-standard WebGL renderer with native GLTFLoader support Input Format DXF (Drawing Exchange Format) Universal CAD interchange standard supported by AutoCAD, Revit, ArchiCAD, SketchUp Output Format glTF / GLB Compact binary 3D scene standard with embedded materials Threading Web Worker (worker.js) Offloads Python execution from the main UI thread so the browser stays responsive Hosting Static site (Netlify) Zero backend cost; no user floor plans leave the client machine

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository.
  2. Place the runtime dependencies (pyodide/, data/, and optionally samples/) inside code/v2-final/ (see code/README.md).
  3. Serve over HTTP (required for Web Workers and WebAssembly): 
    cd code/v2-final/
python3 -m http.server 8080
  4. Open http://localhost:8080 in a modern browser.
  5. Drop a .dxf floor plan or load a sample project.

docs.title: Using the Application
docs.text:
1. Upload — Drag a DXF file onto the upload zone, or click to choose a file.
  2. Process — The Web Worker initializes Pyodide and runs the 4-stage Python pipeline.
  3. Explore — Navigate the generated 3D apartment: - Walk: Drag to look around; click the floor, a room card, or the mini-plan to move; use WASD or arrow keys. - Tour: Automated room-by-room walkthrough; touch or press any key to take manual control. - Views: Keys 1–4 switch camera modes; H toggles the room cards strip.
  4. Customize — Use the side panel to change wall paint colors or select (Click), move (G), rotate (R), add, or delete (Delete) furniture.
  5. Duplex Mode — Upload separate Ground Floor and Upper Floor DXF files to generate a stacked multi-level tour with level-switching controls.

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
• Frontend: React 19, Three.js (GLTFLoader), CSS Custom Properties (light/dark theme)
  • Backend (in-browser): Python 3.12 via Pyodide (WASM)
  • Python Libraries: numpy, networkx, pydantic, pyparsing, fonttools
  • Deployment: Static hosting (Netlify)
  • Documentation: MkDocs Material

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text: VisualEyes runs entirely inside the user's browser. There is no backend server — all DXF parsing, room detection, auto-furnishing, and 3D GLB generation happen client-side using Python compiled to WebAssembly (Pyodide) inside a Web Worker, paired with Three.js on the main thread.

docs.title: 1. User Interface (index.html + app.js)
docs.text:
Built with React 19 and Three.js, featuring a glass-morphism overlay UI:

  • Upload Modal — Drag-and-drop or file picker for single-floor or duplex (Ground + Upper) .dxf files
  • 3D Viewer (#view) — Full-viewport Three.js WebGL canvas with shadow mapping and environment lighting (env/sky.hdr)
  • Room Strip (#strip) — Scrollable room cards with thumbnails and area metrics for one-click navigation
  • Control Island (#island) — Mode switcher for Walk, Orbit, Plan, and Auto-Tour
  • Side Panel — Interactive furniture library, selection gizmos (move/rotate/delete), and custom wall paint color picker
  • Level Selector (#levels) — Floor switcher for duplex projects

docs.title: 2. Web Worker (worker.js)
docs.text:
Isolates the heavy Pyodide WASM runtime from the UI thread:

  • Message Protocol: {id, cmd, args} -> {id, ok, result} (or {id, ok: false, error})
  • Commands:
  • init: Boots Pyodide, loads WASM wheels (numpy, networkx, pydantic, pyparsing, fonttools), unpacks py.zip, and warms pipeline imports
  • parse: Runs ptt_live.parse_dxf on raw DXF bytes
  • edit: Runs ptt_live.edit_plan with user plan corrections
  • build: Runs ptt_live.build_tour and transfers the resulting .glb ArrayBuffer
  • duplex: Runs ptt_live.build_duplex for stacked multi-floor tours
  • Progress Streaming: Emits {progress: {step, done, total}} during initialization

docs.title: 3. Python Pipeline (ptt_*)
docs.text: Module Responsibility ptt_parser Extracts DXF entities (LINE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE, INSERT), constructs wall topology graph via NetworkX, detects & classifies rooms ptt_shell Extrudes 2D wall segments into 3D meshes with parametric door/window cutouts, floors, and ceilings ptt_furnish Places furniture items per room type using spatial constraints, door-swing keepout zones, and proportional scaling ptt_render Assembles the final glTF/GLB binary with PBR materials, textures, and camera/tour metadata

docs.title: 4. Classic Plan Editor (classic.html)
docs.text: A standalone 2D drafting-table editor allowing users to inspect and correct wall geometry or room labels before 3D tour generation.

docs.title: Context Diagram (Level 0 DFD)
docs.text:
The context diagram illustrates VisualEyes as a single system boundary interacting with its external entities.

External Entities:

  • User — Uploads DXF floor plans, customizes furniture/paint, and navigates the 3D tour
  • DXF File — Input 2D CAD floor plan exported from architectural software
  • Browser — Provides WebGL context, Web Workers, and the File API

docs.title: Level 1 DFD
docs.text:
The Level 1 DFD decomposes VisualEyes into its four core processing stages and supporting data stores.

Processes:

  1. P1: Parse DXF (ptt_parser) — Reads binary DXF data, extracts geometric entities, and identifies rooms
  2. P2: Build Shell (ptt_shell) — Extrudes 3D wall, floor, and ceiling geometry from the plan model
  3. P3: Furnish Rooms (ptt_furnish) — Places furniture based on room classification and spatial constraints
  4. P4: Render Tour (ptt_render) — Assembles the GLB 3D scene with PBR materials and camera tour paths

Data Stores:

  • D1: Plan Model — Intermediate JSON representation of walls, openings, and rooms
  • D2: Scene Graph — Combined 3D shell and furniture geometry
  • D3: Furniture Library — Catalog of furniture items, dimensions, and placement rules
  • D4: Material Library — Surface materials, textures, and paint color palettes

docs.title: Level 2 DFD — Parser Subsystem
docs.text:
The Level 2 DFD expands P1 (Parse DXF) into its internal sub-processes.

Sub-processes:

  1. P1.1: Read DXF Entities — Extracts LINE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE, and INSERT entities using layer/block filters
  2. P1.2: Build Wall Graph — Connects line segments into a topological wall graph using NetworkX
  3. P1.3: Detect Room Boundaries — Identifies closed polygons representing individual rooms
  4. P1.4: Classify Rooms — Labels rooms (BEDROOM, KITCHEN, BATHROOM, LIVING, etc.) using area, aspect ratio, and openings

docs.title: Sequence Diagram
docs.text:
End-to-End Execution Flow:

  1. User drops a .dxf file in the UI
  2. UI sends init (first run) and parse commands to worker.js
  3. Web Worker boots Pyodide, loads WASM wheels, and runs ptt_parser
  4. UI receives the parsed Plan JSON and triggers build
  5. Pipeline executes ptt_shell -> ptt_furnish -> ptt_render to produce a .glb file
  6. Worker reads the .glb from Pyodide FS and transfers the ArrayBuffer to the main thread
  7. Three.js parses the GLB with GLTFLoader and renders the interactive 3D tour
